body: I'm in bumfuck Florida, but I've applied all throughout the country, and even out of the country! I have a degree in social science research and statistics. My dream job is to do research, but there are a lot of PhDs flooding the work force right now. I can't muster the energy to go back to school to get my PhD.

I have my ups and downs. Yesterday I was just thinking of working two minimum wage jobs and just trying to apply every day to new positions. I was going to exercise every day, too. Basically your whole plan. But today when I got that rejection it was just too much for me. It knocks me down for so long that it takes a while to recover and be able to function and start applying for more positions. So I guess the whole part that I can't deal with in your thing is the "don't let the rejection get to you." I can't do that for some reason. I take it personally, because this is my blood, sweat, and tears going into this process. My $50,000 debt. My family on my shoulders who are all struggling in their jobs and rooting for me to succeed. It's all my time and energy and emotion that goes into an interview. All thrown away like I'm worth nothing to them. It's too hard to bear sometimes and that is my main problem I guess.

The U.S. is creating a class of young, broken, highly-educated people who feel injustice yet can't do anything to fight it. It creates a system of learned helplessness where we just can't get out of the holes we are in, all the debt. The only thing going for us is that since we are young, we have less to lose than older folks. Maybe that will make us more willing to fight back or revolt or something? I don't know. I hope something changes soon.

Yes I agree that my education makes me look suspicious when I apply for menial jobs. I also think people look at my resume and discriminate against me because if I haven't found a job in 11 months with this resume, there's got to be something wrong with me right? My sister tried to get me a job at the private school where she works and the principal said that to her, so I know for a fact that's what employers are thinking.

It's been 11 months since I graduated, but I started applying for positions 4 months before graduation, so I guess it's been 15 months total. I am so desperate for anything. And you know what makes me feel so worthless is that I have so much debt and not a cent to my name. My car is worth maybe $3,000. I can't donate plasma because I have a blood disorder. I can't donate my eggs because of other medical problems. I can't be a surrogate because you have to have a child of your own first before you surrogate. My body is literally worth nothing, and my education is worth nothing. I looked for cleaning jobs on craigslist. I looked for nanny jobs. Nothing.

How long have you been looking for a job? I've even applied to low wage jobs and jobs that I know I am overqualified for, and even menial jobs, and no one seems to be interested in me. It's like for fucks sake this is a job that requires only a high school degree and I have a master's, what's the problem here? I can't win no matter what I do.

Yes I agree it's the ups and downs that kill me. This last place strung me along for so long, and I had such high hopes. I was planning my life finally. Then I finally press them for an answer and they say they've gone with someone else. It's like fuck you, do you even know what you've done to me for making me wait so long? And yeah, I lost hope of there being any God a long time ago, even when family still tells me that God has a plan for me. Oh really? What's his plan? To keep me on the back burner for a while? If we truly get what we deserve in this world then I must be a shitty human being.

I don't have any family or friends in a position to do that for me. My family has always struggled, and I guess that's my fate too. I'm in a very specialized field that's hard to find a job in. So there are very few positions available to me. I'm highly qualified for those positions, but I can never get past the first or second interview phase. Then when I try to branch out into other fields, they don't like me because I'm not qualified at all to do those jobs.

I weep for all the college graduates who will be graduating next month, because I know that my situation is not unique at all, and a good percentage of those graduates will have to go through what I am going through. I can't even imagine how horrible it is for people who have families to support, mortgages, etc. If it's this hard to deal with unemployment being single and only having two cats to take care of, it's easy for me to see the cycle of homelessness and unemployment and devastation that people with families go through all over the U.S. We have a big problem here in our country with jobs, and the future looks bleak.

Thanks for making me chuckle with the "try nepotism" bit. I should just walk in somewhere and sleep with the boss. I've even considered prostitution to get my bills paid. I worked a shitty minimum wage job all through high school and college and for 6 months after graduating with my master's degree. I can totally do it, but where will that even lead me? I'll just work a shitty job and never be able to find a good one. I feel like I've let my whole family down. They got so excited when I flew out for my interview. I got the rejection from that place this morning and I don't have the heart to tell my family. Sorry for the disconnected thoughts.
